transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Lyndi Kenyon.
Neither Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor political rival Gadi Eisenkot won a clear majority in Israel's election.
Now Israel's president has tapped Eisenkot to form the next Israeli government.
NPR's Lauren Frere has details about Eisenkot.
He's a former military chief whose son was an Israeli soldier killed in combat in Gaza.
He is a center-right politician, while Netanyahu is on the far right.
Eisenkot briefly served in Netanyahu's cabinet after the October 7th Hamas attacks on Israel, but the two had a falling out.
Eisenkot founded a new political party, ran against Netanyahu, and now wants to replace him.
Netanyahu's been Israel's longest-serving prime minister, and he is still the caretaker prime minister for now.
Eisenkot will have six weeks to form a coalition with other political parties.
Democrats who promise to push Medicare for all in states like Michigan, Iowa, and Maine will now have to get the rest of their party on board.
Kate Wells with Kaiser Family Foundation Health News reports that's not going to be an easy sell.
The idea of replacing most or all private health insurance with a single government program, which is what Medicare for All typically means,
Jonathan Oberlander says that is just not going to fly in more conservative states.
He is a health care reform expert at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.
However, if Medicare for All advocates are willing to compromise and carve out a greater role for private insurance,
then you could draw a scenario where you have an AOC as president, big Democratic majorities in the House and Senate.
Is that possible? Yes.
But in the short term, Democrats are likely to focus on trying to get Republican buy-in
for things like restoring tax subsidies for some Obamacare plans.
I'm Kate Wells.
Pope Leo is in Uruguay, where he led an evening prayer vigil.
NPR's Kerry Kahn says the Pope told Uruguayans that Catholics have a role in public life and the church and state can work well together.
Pope Leo hasn't shied away from taking on Uruguay's tightly enforced division between church and state.
In a poor community outside the capital Montevideo, Leo urged more cooperation between the church, civil society and the government to help the poor.
"We must awaken from our inertia and advocate together for the common good," he told a warm but small crowd gathered in Casa Valle, a neighborhood plagued by crime.
Speaking to his largest gathering in Montevideo's historic football stadium, Leo said the government does have a role,
but nothing compares to God's love, which is stronger, he said, than hate, violence and war.
Kerry Kahn, NPR News, Montevideo.
You're listening to NPR.
Millions around the world are celebrating Diwali, which is one of India's biggest holidays.
NPR's Shandalese Duster reports on the celebrations in the U.S.
Known as the Festival of Lights, Diwali began in India more than 2,000 years ago.
While it is a major Hindu festival, it's also celebrated by other religions such as Jains and Sikhs.
With more than 5 million people of Indian origin living in the U.S., more and more cities are hosting public events
to celebrate what's known as the victory of light over darkness.
In downtown Seattle, community groups offered free vegetarian meals, classical Indian dancing and cow cuddling.
There were celebrations on the East Coast, including in Edison, New Jersey, where there was also food, dancing and 100,000 lights on display.
Shandalese Duster, NPR News.
Tesla's Cybertruck will soon be a thing of the past. Tesla CEO Elon Musk says the company will cease production next year.
Musk said the move was meant to allow increased production of the CyberCab robotaxi.
In a post on social media, he added production will be winding down around the middle of next year.
Production has been centered at the Tesla facility outside Austin, Texas.
The large stainless steel Cybertruck with its unique design was once Tesla's signature product.
It sparked both praise and derision for its very unusual style, including what was sometimes described as its science fiction appearance.
I'm Linda Kenyon, NPR News, in Washington.

Democrats pushing Medicare for All in Michigan, Iowa, and Maine face hard sell to party and conservative states
Pope Leo visits Uruguay, urges church, civil society and government cooperation for the poor at evening vigil
Diwali celebrated across the U.S., with public events in Seattle and Edison, New Jersey
Elon Musk says Tesla will end Cybertruck production next year to expand CyberCab robotaxi output
